author: woosh
body:
This PR changes some regular expressions for matching function names. It addresses two problems:

1. Matching function name in generated contracts. The previous version looked for the string `/* contracts for ... */`. However, in an upcoming version of TriCera the relevant line is `/* contract for ... */` (note the removed plural "s"). This version will accept both.
2. Matching a function name in the input source. The previous version relied on the function declaration being on a single line. More specifically it relied on the closing bracket being available on the same line as the function name. However, in real world sources this is not always the case. This version will in addition accept a declaration that starts on one line but doesn't necessarily have the closing bracket on the same line.
3. Fix Frama-C to version 29. (Required to make sure same version of Frama-C is used in OCaml 4 and 5 track)

The entry points of python scripts with a hardcoded absolute path to python, this is not portable. On linux/macos they contain a shebang which we can patch (we already do), on windows, this is an executable which is harder to patch post-build. Others (e.g. conda) does this during installation but we don't have an install step with vcpkg when fetching packages from caches.
Ideally this path should be relative to the executable, how this can be done needs more investigation.
What we do here is, creating a wrapper .bat file that calls python with the main entry point as an alternative to the exe (the exe is still present!)

body:
I chose this approach - to refuse/block the broadcast of the proposal - as it has the least impact on the rest of the code, as opposed to checking/failing at every step of the proposal assembly. So, a node is allowed to go thru the motions of assembling a proposal but will only broadcast a proposal if-and-only-if it is in-sync at the time of broadcast.

In addition, the proposer checks that the proposed block is not lagging the chain, to address the situation where the node might have been out-of-sync at the start of proposal assembly but caught up by the time it had to broadcast the proposal.

The proposal itself could very well be a fork, and that is dealt with elsewhere, as usual.

a xenobiology setup (ie, the console/smartfridge/slime grinder) was moved to the second layer of icebox, because slimes do not follow their ai when no one is on their z level. the option to be on either level is now available.

icebox xenobio is very difficult to maintain without either running up and down the stairs while your slimes feed, or moving the entire setup to the second layer. this will allow lowpop scientists to be able to handle their slimes with ease

author: copilot
body:
The BasicKernel project was not working with the latest version of Semantic Kernel (1.11.1) because the API for `InvokePromptAsync` has changed to require execution settings.

Changes made:
1. Added `OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings` to configure execution parameters
2. Updated `InvokePromptAsync` call to use the new parameter format required by the latest version
3. Added clear comments explaining why the execution settings are needed
4. Updated commented example code to maintain consistency with the new API requirements

**Before:**
```csharp
var prompt = "What are the things to do in Utrecht?";
var response = await kernel.InvokePromptAsync(prompt);
```

**After:**
```csharp
var prompt = "What are the things to do in Utrecht?";
// Create execution settings for OpenAI - required in newer versions of Semantic Kernel
OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings openAIPromptExecutionSettings = new();
// Pass execution settings to the invoke method
var response = await kernel.InvokePromptAsync(prompt, new(openAIPromptExecutionSettings));
```

This change aligns with the working code pattern in other projects like KernelWithPlugin.

Fixes #1.

This pull request introduces multiple updates to improve functionality, enhance error handling, and update documentation for a GitHub Action that manages labels on pull requests or issues. Key changes include refining the workflow YAML file, updating the `README.md` to reflect the new label format, improving error handling in the `remove-labels.sh` script, and removing outdated code.

### Workflow Updates:
* Updated `.github/workflows/test-workflow.yml` to support adding and removing multiple labels, as well as single labels, with clearer step names. Added a new step to handle removing labels that are not present. ### Documentation Updates:
* Revised `README.md` to remove references to custom delimiters for labels and updated the example usage to reflect the new YAML array format for labels. Added a footer with a personal touch.

### Script Enhancements:
* Improved `remove-labels.sh` by adding a check for the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable to ensure it is set before proceeding.
* Enhanced error handling in `remove-labels.sh` by adding specific messages for HTTP status codes (e.g., 404 for "Label not found," 403 for "Forbidden," and 422 for "Unprocessable Entity").

* Removed outdated comments and code in `remove-labels.sh`, such as the delimiter-based label parsing logic, since the new YAML array format is now used.
